steps.title: Excel & Spreadsheet Analysis
steps.subtitle: Clean, summarise and chart data in spreadsheets
steps.description: Excel is still the first tool most analyst interviews and jobs test. Learn the formulas, lookups and PivotTables that turn raw exports into clean summaries, and build cleaning steps you can repeat and trust.

topics.name: Core formulas and cell references: relative, absolute ($A$1) and mixed; SUM, AVERAGE, ROUND
Logical and conditional functions: IF/IFS, AND/OR, IFERROR, COUNTIFS, SUMIFS and AVERAGEIFS
Lookups and dynamic arrays: VLOOKUP (exact vs approximate match), INDEX/MATCH, XLOOKUP, FILTER and UNIQUE
PivotTables and PivotCharts: grouping, Show Values As (% of total), slicers and refresh
Data cleaning: TRIM and text functions, Remove Duplicates, Text to Columns, data validation and Power Query
Excel Tables, sorting and filtering, and formula-based conditional formatting
Charts in Excel: choosing column, line, bar, scatter and combo charts with clear titles and labels

steps.title: SQL for Analysis
steps.subtitle: Query, join and aggregate data at the source
steps.description: Most company data lives in relational databases, and SQL rounds are standard in analyst interviews. Learn to filter, aggregate and join tables correctly, handle NULLs and dates, and use CTEs and window functions for rankings, running totals and month-over-month comparisons.

topics.name: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT and DISTINCT with IN, BETWEEN and LIKE filters
Aggregation with COUNT/SUM/AVG, GROUP BY and HAVING, and the logical order of query execution
Joins: INNER, LEFT and self joins, and avoiding duplicated rows (fan-out) from one-to-many keys
Subqueries and CTEs (WITH) for multi-step analysis
Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK/DENSE_RANK, LAG/LEAD and running totals with SUM() OVER
NULL handling (IS NULL, COALESCE, NULLIF) and CASE WHEN for conditional logic
Date functions: DATE_TRUNC, EXTRACT, date arithmetic and month-over-month comparisons

steps.title: Statistics for Data Analysis
steps.subtitle: Draw conclusions you can defend
steps.description: Statistics tells you whether a pattern is real or just noise. Learn to summarise distributions, spot sampling bias and confounders, run and interpret hypothesis tests and confidence intervals, and design A/B tests that product teams can rely on.

topics.name: Descriptive statistics: mean, median, mode, standard deviation, percentiles and IQR
Distributions: normal (68-95-99.7 rule), binomial, skewness, outliers and the central limit theorem
Sampling methods and bias: random vs stratified samples, selection and survivorship bias
Correlation vs causation: Pearson/Spearman correlation, confounders and Simpson's paradox
Hypothesis testing: p-values, Type I/II errors, confidence intervals, t-tests and chi-square tests
Regression basics: linear regression, R² and logistic regression for yes/no outcomes
A/B testing: randomisation, sample size and power, peeking and multiple comparisons

steps.title: Python for Data Analysis
steps.subtitle: Wrangle and explore data with Pandas
steps.description: Python with Pandas handles datasets that are too large or messy for spreadsheets and makes your analysis reproducible. Learn to load, clean, reshape and merge data in Jupyter, write fast vectorised code, and explore it visually with Matplotlib and Seaborn.

topics.name: Python essentials for analysis (lists, dicts, functions) in Jupyter Notebook or Google Colab
Pandas DataFrames: read_csv, loc/iloc selection, boolean filtering and sorting
Cleaning data: dtypes, .str methods, pd.to_datetime, pd.to_numeric and duplicates
Missing values: isna, dropna, fillna and when to impute versus drop
Aggregating and combining: groupby/agg/transform, pivot_table, melt, merge and concat
Vectorised operations with NumPy/Pandas instead of row-by-row loops (apply, iterrows)
Visualisation with Matplotlib and Seaborn: histograms, box plots, scatter plots and heatmaps

steps.title: BI Dashboards & Data Storytelling
steps.subtitle: Turn analysis into decisions
steps.description: Insights only matter when decision-makers understand and act on them. Learn to model data and write DAX measures in Power BI (or build the same in Tableau), design clear KPI dashboards, run cohort and funnel analyses, and present findings as a short story that ends in a recommendation.

topics.name: Power BI or Tableau basics: connecting data, Power Query, visuals, filters and slicers
Data modelling: star schema, fact vs dimension tables, relationships and a dedicated date table
DAX basics: measures vs calculated columns, CALCULATE, filter context and time intelligence
KPI design: clear definitions, targets and comparisons, ratio of totals vs average of ratios
Dashboard best practices: chart choice, layout, colour and honest axes
Product analytics: cohort retention, funnel conversion and churn analysis
Communicating insights: lead with the so-what, executive summaries and recommendations
